questions.stem: A 12 V ideal DC source is connected in series with a 4 Ω resistor (R1). The output of that series combination feeds a parallel combination of a 6 Ω resistor (R2) and a 12 Ω resistor (R3), and the parallel combination returns to the source's negative terminal, completing the circuit. What is the total current supplied by the source?
questions.explanation: First reduce the parallel pair: R23 = (R2 R3)/(R2 + R3) = (6)(12)/(6+12) = 72/18 = 4 Ω. This combines in series with R1: R_eq = R1 + R23 = 4 + 4 = 8 Ω. By Ohm's law, I = V/R_eq = 12 V / 8 Ω = 1.5 A. (Choice D results from ignoring R1 and using only R23; choice A and C do not satisfy Ohm's law for this network.)
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook, Electrical and Computer Engineering — "Resistors in Series and Parallel" (p. 363)

questions.stem: The current through a circuit element is given by i(t) = 14.14 cos(377t + 30°) A. What are the RMS value of the current and the frequency of the waveform?
questions.explanation: For a sinusoid, X_rms = X_max/√2. Here I_max = 14.14 A, so I_rms = 14.14/√2 = 10.0 A. The angular frequency is ω = 377 rad/s, and f = ω/(2π) = 377/6.2832 = 60.0 Hz. (Choice A confuses peak with RMS; choice C mistakes ω for f; choice D incorrectly halves the peak value as for a half-wave rectified signal.)
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook, Electrical and Computer Engineering — "AC Circuits": Average Value and Effective or RMS Values (p. 365)

questions.stem: At node A of a resistive DC circuit, a 3 A ideal current source injects current into the node. Node A is also connected to a 24 V source through a 6 Ω resistor (R1), to ground through a 12 Ω resistor (R2), and to ground through a 4 Ω resistor (R3). Using Kirchhoff's current law (KCL) at node A, determine the node voltage V_A.
questions.explanation: Sum currents entering node A and set equal to currents leaving: 3 + (24 − V_A)/6 = V_A/12 + V_A/4. Multiply through by 12: 36 + 2(24 − V_A) = V_A + 3V_A, so 36 + 48 − 2V_A = 4V_A, giving 84 = 6V_A, so V_A = 14.0 V. Check: current in = 3 + (24−14)/6 = 3 + 1.667 = 4.667 A; current out = 14/12 + 14/4 = 1.167 + 3.5 = 4.667 A. KCL balances.
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook, Electrical and Computer Engineering — "Kirchhoff's Laws" (p. 363)

questions.stem: A 30 V ideal DC source is connected in series with a 6 Ω resistor (R1) to node a. From node a, a 12 Ω resistor (R2) and a 4 Ω resistor (R3) each connect back to the source's negative terminal, which is node b (R2 and R3 are in parallel with each other between nodes a and b). A load will be attached across terminals a-b. Determine the Thévenin equivalent voltage V_oc and equivalent resistance R_eq seen by the load.
questions.explanation: With the load removed, node a is a voltage divider: R2 ∥ R3 = (12)(4)/(12+4) = 48/16 = 3 Ω. V_oc = 30 V × 3/(6+3) = 30 × 1/3 = 10 V. To find R_eq, deactivate the source (short it), which places R1, R2, and R3 all in parallel between a and b: R_eq = 1/(1/6 + 1/12 + 1/4) = 1/(2/12 + 1/12 + 3/12) = 1/(6/12) = 2 Ω. (Choice D incorrectly adds R1 in series with R2∥R3 = 6+3 = 9 Ω instead of placing all three in parallel after deactivation.)
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook, Electrical and Computer Engineering — "Source Equivalents" (p. 363)

questions.stem: A series RLC circuit consists of a 30 Ω resistor, a 106.1 mH inductor, and a 33.2 µF capacitor, all in series across an AC source v(t) = 120√2 cos(377t) V (i.e., V_rms = 120∠ 0° V at f = 60 Hz). Determine the RMS magnitude and phase angle of the current phasor, and state whether the current leads or lags the source voltage.

choices.A: I = 2.4 A∠ 53.13°, current leads the voltage
choices.B: I = 2.4 A∠ −53.13°, current lags the voltage
choices.C: I = 4.0 A∠ 36.87°, current leads the voltage
choices.D: I = 1.5 A∠ 53.13°, current leads the voltage

questions.explanation: At ω = 2π(60) = 377 rad/s: X_L = ωL = 377(0.1061) = 40.0 Ω, and X_C = 1/(ωC) = 1/[377(33.2×10⁻⁶)] = 80.0 Ω. The series impedance is Z = R + j(X_L − X_C) = 30 + j(40 − 80) = 30 − j40 Ω = 50∠−53.13° Ω. Since X_C > X_L, the circuit is net capacitive, and Z has a negative angle. The current phasor is I = V/Z = 120∠0° / 50∠−53.13° = 2.4∠+53.13° A rms. Because the impedance angle is negative (capacitive), the current phasor leads the voltage phasor by 53.13°.
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook, Electrical and Computer Engineering — "Phasor Transforms of Sinusoids" and Impedance table (p. 366)

questions.stem: An ideal battery (96 V), a 4 A current source, and three resistors (4 Ohm, 4 Ohm, 6 Ohm) are assembled in a circuit. Using superposition, most nearly what is the current flowing through the 6 Ohm resistor?
questions.explanation:
Use superposition.

Step 1 (voltage source only):
Total R = 4 + (4||6) = 4 + 2.4 = 6.4 Ohm
I_total = 96/6.4 = 15 A
I_6 = 15 x [4/(4+6)] = 6 A

Step 2 (current source only):
4||4 = 2 Ohm
I_6 = 4 x [2/(6+2)] = 1 A

Total = 6 + 1 = 7 A

questions.stem: A circuit with two terminals has a 30 mA current source and two 3 kOhm resistors. The Thevenin equivalent across terminals A and B is
questions.explanation:
Thevenin voltage:
V_th = (30 mA)(3 kOhm) = 90 V

Thevenin resistance (zero current source = open):
R_th = 3 kOhm + 3 kOhm = 6 kOhm

Equivalent: 90 V in series with 6 kOhm

questions.stem: A circuit has a 10 V source, 4 A current source, and resistors of 2 Ohm and 3 Ohm. Converting the current source and 3 Ohm to a Thevenin equivalent, most nearly the current through the 2 Ohm resistor is
questions.explanation:
Convert 4 A source || 3 Ohm:
V_oc = (3)(4) = 12 V (Thevenin)

I = (12 - 10)/(2 + 3) = 0.4 A
12 V > 10 V => current flows right to left.

questions.stem: A meter movement has internal resistance 5 kOhm and full-scale current 50 uA. For a voltmeter with full-scale voltage 20 V, the series resistance required is most nearly
questions.explanation:
Total resistance:
R_total = V_fs / I_fs = 20 V / 50e-6 = 400 kOhm

Series resistance:
R_series = 400 kOhm - 5 kOhm = 395 kOhm ~= 400 kOhm

questions.stem: A voltmeter connected in parallel with a resistor requires its internal resistance to be ___ for an accurate voltage reading.

choices.A: much smaller than the measured resistance
choices.B: approximately equal to the measured resistance
choices.D: much greater than the measured resistance

questions.explanation:
The voltmeter is in parallel with the load. If its resistance is too low, it draws excessive current and disturbs the measurement.

For accurate reading: R_voltmeter >> R_load
This minimizes the loading effect.

questions.stem: A circuit has a 10 V source and resistors of 2 Ohm, 10 Ohm, and 15 Ohm. Most nearly, what value of load R_L allows maximum power transfer?
questions.explanation:
Maximum power transfer: R_L = R_Thevenin

R_Th = 2 + (10||15) = 2 + 6 = 8.0 Ohm
